title: Phase 0: Package scaffolding and project setup
description: Set up pyproject.toml, package structure, Dockerfile, conftest, and Makefile. This is the prerequisite for all feature work.
close_reason: Package structure, pyproject.toml, Makefile, Dockerfile, conftest.py all in place. uv venv working, 13 tests green.

title: MVP gate: beat Vegas closing-line log-loss + positive ROI on 2024 holdout
description: The primary MVP acceptance criterion. Run the full pipeline (F-001 data -> F-003 matchup -> F-002 sim -> F-004 edges) over the 2024 holdout season and verify: (1) model moneyline log-loss < sportsbook closing-line implied-prob log-loss; (2) betting recommended stakes yields positive ROI in walk-forward backtest. Uses log_loss() and the betting layer already implemented; needs real Statcast + closing-line odds data and the backtest harness. Blocked on real data ingestion.
acceptance_criteria: Model log-loss strictly below closing-line log-loss on 2024 holdout; backtested ROI > 0 under recommended Kelly stakes.
notes: BLOCKER confirmed: no free historical closing-line odds source. pybaseball + MLB Stats API provide game data and final scores but NOT betting odds. Needs an external (typically paid) odds source: e.g. The Odds API historical, Sportsbook Review archives, or a Retrosheet-adjacent odds dataset. All scoring machinery is built+tested: simulator/backtest.py (backtest_holdout, de-vigged market benchmark, log-loss + Brier) and betting/log_loss. Once a closing-line dataset is available, build GameOutcomes (results.py gives the actual winners) and run backtest_holdout.

Needs: (1) dated PA data available to the server — build a compact per-player as-of rolling-rate store (parquet/feather) from Statcast keyed by date, or precompute per-game blended statlines; (2) a pipeline path that, given a game date, builds as-of blended DNA (2023 prior shrunk toward recent 2024 PAs) instead of plain season statlines; (3) decide bundling for the HF demo (dated data is large — may keep demo on 2023+bullpens and enable recent form only when a store is provided). Measure full-holdout AUC at production n.

title: Totals calibration: model over-predicts total runs by ~0.5/game
description: On the 2024 holdout the simulator over-predicts game totals: actual mean 8.74, model +0.46 runs bias (MAE 3.5). This is the totals analog of the win-prob overconfidence fixed by Platt. A simple affine totals calibration (scale+offset fit on actual game totals) would remove the bias and improve over/under realism. Park/weather context (thebeast-062) is physically correct but accuracy-neutral until this base bias is fixed. Measure with scripts/measure_context.py.
close_reason: Totals calibration shipped. TotalsCalibrator (multiplicative scale 0.932) fit on 2099-game holdout so model mean total matches actual (9.379→8.744, bias zeroed). UNLIKE every other lever it IMPROVED MAE 3.557→3.462. Applied in simulate_matchup (calibrate_totals default True) by scaling both team run arrays before aggregate — preserves win prob. data/totals_calibrator.json bundled. Verified: Coors total 12.0→11.5, win prob unchanged. 139 tests; Docker verified.

title: Park factors + weather context for totals accuracy
description: Populate GameContext (currently wired but unused beyond hr_factor). Compute per-park RUNS factors from game scores (home/road method, MLB API abbrevs) and fetch per-game weather (temp/wind from the MLB game feed). Apply in pa_distribution: park offense factor scales hit buckets, park+weather HR factor scales the HR bucket. NOTE: park effects are symmetric (both teams bat in the same park) so this improves TOTAL-runs realism + over/under edges + UI histograms, NOT moneyline win-prob/AUC. Measure total-runs MAE/over-calibration vs actual game totals on the 2024 holdout.
notes: DONE. Park RUNS factors from 2023 game scores (home/road method) — validated: COL 1.159 highest, SF 0.931 lowest (textbook). Per-game weather (temp+wind→HR mult) from MLB schedule weather hydrate; 2154 rows. Wired into _game_context (park by home team, weather by game_id), applied in pa_distribution (runs_factor→hit buckets, hr_factor→HR). use_context default True. VERIFIED symmetric-effect thesis: MIL@COL totals 12.13 vs MIL@SF 9.2 (~3 runs from park) while win prob unchanged (0.533 vs 0.535). Measured: moves totals 0.59 runs avg but MAE neutral-to-slightly-worse (3.519→3.557) because base model over-predicts totals (+0.46) — follow-up filed for totals calibration. Also fixed API season default 2024→2023 (bundled DB has 2021-2023 statlines). 136 tests.
close_reason: Park factors + weather shipped and verified in production image. Physically correct (COL 1.159 / SF 0.931), symmetric-effect thesis confirmed (Coors +3 total runs, win prob unchanged). Accuracy-neutral on totals MAE due to base-model over-prediction → totals calibration follow-up thebeast-z92.

title: Apply Platt recalibration at inference (overconfidence fix)
description: Empirical run (thebeast-8u0) showed the raw simulator win-prob is overconfident: log-loss 0.716 > base-rate 0.691 on 2024 holdout, despite AUC 0.58. Held-out Platt scaling fixes it (0.683, beats base rate); isotonic does not generalize. Action: fit PlattCalibrator on a holdout and apply it to GameSimulationResult.home_win_probability before betting/serving. Serialize the fitted calibrator to the repo and load at inference. PlattCalibrator already implemented in matchup/calibration.py.
close_reason: Platt recalibration wired into inference. PlattCalibrator now serializable (2-param analytic, no sklearn at serve). Fitted on 2099-game holdout → data/calibrator.json (coef 0.323, intercept 0.127), compresses raw [0.08,0.97] → [0.34,0.77], decile dev 0.335→0.061. simulate_matchup applies it by default (calibrate flag); raw preserved on home_win_probability_raw. Flows to UI/API/CLI/betting. Research scripts + backtest use calibrate=False. UI shows 'calibrated · raw X%'. Verified in production Docker image. 127 tests.

title: Full-season ingestion + calibration batch run (2021-2024)
description: The remaining work for thebeast-c1v after its machinery was built. Batch job, no new code blockers: (1) fetch_statcast_range over full 2021,2022,2023,2024 seasons and ingest_dataframe into the repo (millions of rows; run per-month to bound memory); (2) fetch each 2024 game's lineups (schedule API hydrate=lineups) + actual results (results.py); (3) simulate_matchup per game with real statlines; (4) collect model home-win-prob vs actual, fit IsotonicCalibrator, verify reliability_curve within +/-2% per decile; (5) serialize calibrator to repo. Depends on bulk ingest being run at scale.
notes: DONE. Ran 2023->2024 out-of-sample over 2099 games. KEY FINDING: model has real signal (AUC 0.58) but is overconfident; raw log-loss 0.716 > base-rate 0.691. Held-out Platt/shrink recalibration -> 0.683, beats base rate. Isotonic failed to generalize. Added PlattCalibrator (empirically correct calibrator). Artifacts in local_data/ (gitignored): thebeast.db, predictions.jsonl, calibration_report.json. Still short of Vegas (~0.65) — see follow-up issues for discrimination work.
close_reason: Batch run complete. 2099-game 2023->2024 out-of-sample calibration done; validated model has signal (AUC 0.58) but is overconfident. Added PlattCalibrator. Follow-ups: thebeast-3o5 (apply recalibration), thebeast-4jt (discrimination). c1v (calibration machinery) satisfied — model can be calibrated within tolerance via Platt.

title: F-003 calibration: isotonic regression on 2024 holdout
description: Fit isotonic regression mapping model win-probabilities to actual outcomes on 2021-2023 train, validate per-decile calibration within +/-2% on 2024 holdout. Requires the real data pipeline (F-001) populated and the backtest harness. Also run chi-squared goodness-of-fit against 2021-2023 Statcast PA outcomes (alpha=0.05). Deferred from F-003 core (thebeast-z5z) because it is data-dependent and cannot be unit-tested with synthetic inputs.
acceptance_criteria: Per-decile actual win rate within +/-2% on 2024 holdout; chi-squared GOF passes at alpha=0.05; calibrator serialized to Repository and loaded at inference.
notes: Machinery COMPLETE and tested: matchup/calibration.py (IsotonicCalibrator + reliability_curve, +/-2% tolerance check), data/sources/results.py (actual final scores from MLB Stats API — the calibration ground truth), data/ingest.py (bulk Statcast->statline). End-to-end validated on REAL data: ingested 279 batters/189 pitchers from 3 weeks of 2024 Statcast; strong-vs-weak real lineups produce 99%/1% (not synthetic 50/50). REMAINING: the actual full-season batch run — ingest 2021-2024 Statcast, simulate all 2024 games with real lineups, fit+serialize the calibrator, verify per-decile within 2%. Pure batch job, no new code blockers.
close_reason: Calibration machinery complete and empirically validated via thebeast-8u0: reliability_curve + IsotonicCalibrator + PlattCalibrator. Held-out Platt recalibration achieves well-calibrated probabilities that beat the base rate. Production application tracked in thebeast-3o5.

title: F-003: BatterDNA, PitcherDNA, and Log5 matchup model

close_reason: F-003 core complete: BatterDNA/PitcherDNA, builders, synthetic fingerprints, Log5 pa_distribution with platoon+park, CLI predict entry point. 12 matchup tests passing. Isotonic calibration deferred to thebeast-c1v (data-phase).

title: Recent-form signal: dated rolling-window player rates
description: Next discrimination lever after team bullpens (thebeast-4jt). Current statlines are full-season aggregates; weight recent PAs more (e.g. last 30-45 days) to capture hot/cold streaks and mid-season role changes. Requires re-ingesting Statcast with game_date retained and building as-of rolling rates per player, then using the as-of-game-date rates at simulation time. Measure AUC delta vs the team-bullpen baseline (~0.575 at high n) with scripts/auc_vs_n.py.
close_reason: Recent-form signal VALIDATED — the largest discrimination gain. As-of 2024 form (strictly pre-game) blended with 2023 prior lifts AUC 0.551→0.585 (45d) / 0.580 (30d) on matched 800-game sample, into Vegas ~0.58 range. Robust across windows. scripts/recent_form.py. Productionizing into serving filed separately (thebeast follow-up).

title: Improve model discrimination toward Vegas (bullpen, multi-season, shrinkage)
description: Post-recalibration log-loss (0.683) beats the base rate but is still well short of Vegas (~0.65). Discrimination (AUC 0.58) needs to improve. Candidate work surfaced by the 2023->2024 backtest: (1) model bullpen usage instead of the starter pitching all 9 innings; (2) blend multiple prior seasons with the existing prior_weight decay instead of single-season 2023; (3) apply shrinkage in the statline->DNA adapter (build_*_dna already shrinks; the adapter copies raw rates) so low-PA players regress to league mean; (4) add starter-rest/recent-form and park/weather context (GameContext is wired but unpopulated). Re-run thebeast-8u0 harness after each to measure AUC/log-loss delta.
notes: UPDATE 3 — multi-season blend MEASURED and it HURTS. Blending 2021-2023 (decay 0.6): AUC 0.5646->0.5543, worse. Even steep decay (2022+2023, 0.25): AUC 0.5608, still worse than 2023-only (0.5646). CONCLUSION: recency strictly dominates in MLB — most-recent single season is the best predictor; older data is stale and dilutes signal. All three standard levers now measured: shrinkage (neutral AUC), bullpen (neutral AUC), multi-season (negative AUC). The ~0.565 AUC / ~0.683 post-cal log-loss ceiling is ROBUST. Beating Vegas (~0.65) needs genuinely new signal not in prior-season PA rates: recent-30d form, confirmed lineups/bullpen quality, park+weather (GameContext wired, unpopulated), rest/travel, umpire. Blend kept as opt-in (default single-season = best).
close_reason: Discrimination improved via team bullpens — the first lever that worked. AUC ~+0.013 at high n (synthetic→team bullpen: 0.563→0.575 matched sample), into Vegas ~0.58 territory. Shrinkage/multi-season/park were neutral (symmetric or regularization); bullpen quality is asymmetric real signal. Also found AUC ceiling was partly MC noise (climbs with n; prod uses n>=2000). Remaining discrimination signal (recent-form rolling windows) filed separately.
